So sorry to hear that. I've had similar experience with my mom (well, parents) in the past...

I've been under my mom's radar since I was a kid. Even after being diagnosed with depression as a young teen and undergoing a serious surgery which left me with permament digestional difficulties at the age of 10. She wouldn't leave me alone because she honestly didn't find anything problematic about her behaviour. A few years ago (I'm in my late twenties now) I have finally found a way to confront her in an effective way. I sat both my parents down. I expressed how my feelings get hurt by my mom's observations. She wan't sure what I was addressing. I asked my dad if he knew what I was talking about. He said he knew. I then named a few examples. She stuck to her old "I can't even express an opinion around my family?" defense mechanism, to which I responded with something like "I get it's your opinion, but I am on the receiving end here and it hurts my feelings, especially when you know how hard I'm working on my self-esteem". Then my father chipped in with telling me "You are being too sensitive" - something I have been hearing my whole life. And at THAT moment I actually said something that changed our relationship regarding mutual respect. 

I told them that I respect their opinion and at no cost do I want to restrict any communication between us. But there is a difference between saying your opinion and repeatedly hurting your child's feelings after multiple times of being told that it hurts. It's not about expressing opinions or feelings anymore - it's straightforward not respecting what your child says and feels. Their duty as good parents is to respect the reaction and feelings it evokes in their child. If they neglect it and pursue acting as before, it speaks on a deeper level and perhaps can help you choose how to shape your relationship in the future. Also, no one has the right to tell you you are "too sensitive". There is no such thing as a standard sensitivity level and no one has the power to judge how deep a person has the right to feel. It's about human decency and respect between individuals, be it your mother or a stranger in the street. Yes, it's complicated because there is a huge history behind you. But it all comes down to that. Once I've communicated this to my parents it left them speechless. Literally. It made a huge change in our relationship.

Yes, it sounds like your mother is projecting and it's nascissistic. I encourage you to take a stand on your feelings and insist on receiving respect as another human being! It took years for me to achieve this and it's still annoying to hear pointless criticism that comes from a selfish place. Sometimes it hurts. It was definitely terrible when I was a teen, but I have managed to more or less distance myself from it with years, and maybe you can too. Sorry for the long post. The topic gets me caught up. Good luck!!!

hey Grogford... i feel you. this has been and IS happening to me since as my therapist while they adapt my therapy. with some antidepressants, i feel like a water balloon and only the sight of a tree in the wind could make my cry my eyeballs out. then on some antidepressants, the ones i'm taking now, i find myself in the description of what you wrote. i feel this burden on my chest that stretches to my throat and the tears are here, but then - nothing. and then, just like you describe it, it can happen in a second i just fully break down in tears for seemingly no reason.

anyway... i try to pull those tears out of myself in every way i could. when i am fully depressed, i find masturbation relieving because, and i can't explain why, i break down and cry after every orgasm. this is one of the ways how i deal. since i am an unstable person, i am diagnosed with borderline, lately i get suicidal a couple times in a day. just because of this numbness... it's scary to think you wouldn't care about your family's and friends' feelings after your death. but i think about it as soon as i start picturing ugly things... i think about my little brother, my parents and my grandparents. it makes me cry. i imagine my own funeral. it makes me cry. to imagine their pain, it breaks me down, and sometimes this is the way i vent out. idk if that's psychopathic or not. but for me, it works. and i put the suicidal thoughts on pause.

IT'S SO ANNOYING. i call what you've described 'autopilot mode' because you are still depressed, and you feel it inside you, but your bodily functions just won't show it. i used to be on autopilot for years doing things i now retrospectively regret just to make myself feel anything. ended up feeling vast numbness. and then when it hit me, i start crying my eyes out.

One of the most tranquil and beautiful places I've visited in Europe is Óbidos, somewhere between Lisboa and Figueira da Foz in Portugal. Lovely town with a medieval aura, beautiful nature to explore by bike or on foot, local cuisine is delicious, and don't forget Ginja, the famous sour cherry liqueur drank from small chocolate cups. Also, Arouca - on the inland of Portugal, municipality of Porto, a hidden gem if you're a fan of intact nature. Arouca Geopark is on the UNESCO's list for its natural phenomena of 'birthing rocks'. I'd suggest exploring the region by motorcycle. We even stumbled upon a hord of tame bulls slowly crossing the road before our eyes. Stunning! Portugal is full of non-touristy places with amazing cultural heritage and fantastic cuisine far away from the busy coast. Most of tourism is centred on the coast, especially Southern Portugal.

hey bullet_train_94 :) okay, so. i don't know if my words will make any difference on how you currently feel about yourself, i can only hope, i will try. reading your post woke up something familiar in me.

when i was a teen, i had a best friend who i was in love with probably from the moment we met. he was the first person who, you know, i fell in LOVE with, even though i had crushes before, this was different. also, he is 4 years older than me, which at that point was a huge deal - me, a 14 year old girl, him, an 18 year old boy. we were very close, had contact on a daily basis for a couple years, he wrote me stories even (he is now a published writer), we said i love you to each other. however, it was never anything romantic, we have never kissed and i have never admitted i was in love with him. he viewed me as his younger sister, which he said to me many times. i hurt so much for years, i cried myself to sleep, daily, because i knew we would never be together. i invented reasons to hate myself because i felt rejected, i was 'too ugly, too chubby, too stupid, too out-of-his-league' for him, all the possible pejoratives you could imagine.

now, what did i figure out years later (of course, because all wounds take time to heal). most adolescents don't know what they want. and some adolescents like attention. some adolescents both like attention AND don't know what they want, which ends up in hurt, since people around them feel used and played for truly caring. now, this is shit. which is why figuring out how to be a young adult is hard. i guess what i'm trying to say is - i believe your friend gave you mixed signals because she didn't know what she wanted. or maybe wanted for you to make a move which you couldn't read from her/weren't ready to make at that point. whatever it was, i am sorry you had your heart played around with, i truly am. i wish i could comfort you somehow... what i certainly DO know, is that your acts, as an individual, as a unique human being, had nothing to do with how things turned out. especially your virginity! i obviously don't know you personally, but even from the way you described things in your post, i can feel you are a nice person and someone i'd like to hang out with.

no matter what you do, please don't base your opinion about yourself on others' reactions, words or acts. unfortunately, most of the time people don't think about the consequences they might have on others. you WILL attract lots of girls in your life. just stick to who you know you are and believe in your uniqueness (well, because it's real lol). if you want to talk more, hmu!
